clue.text: Out of harm's way, a sodden faun's given treatment

indicators.note: something given treatment is worked on and changed, so these letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: every letter of these words, including the possessive S, is the fodder

explanation.surface: A soaked faun, rescued from danger, is being cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who has come through danger unhurt, which is exactly being clear of peril.

clue.text: Eminent scientist makes you think when page's turned

indicators.note: turned suggests being twisted around, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: all fourteen letters, the possessive S included, are the fodder

explanation.surface: A great scientist's book gives readers food for thought with every page they turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to describe reading a science book, but the words from 'think' to 'page's' are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawking was a celebrated British theoretical physicist, famous for black hole research and A Brief History of Time.

clue.text: Pale, shuddering, overcome by convulsion in infested locale

indicators.note: being overcome by something means being engulfed, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a fit is a sudden convulsion

indicators.note: something shuddering is shaken about, so its letters get jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pale and shaking with a seizure in a bug-ridden place.
explanation.walkthrough: A fleapit is British slang for a shabby, run-down cinema, supposedly crawling with fleas.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term names a dingy cinema or venue imagined to harbour fleas, so a place full of pests.

clue.text: PS: Tipsy dad and mummy regularly hugging, close

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping arms around, so the outer pieces enclose another

parts.note: the word dad rearranged

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so the word after it is jumbled

parts.note: the close of something is its end

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of mummy

explanation.surface: A postscript reporting that drunken dad and mum keep cuddling up close.
explanation.walkthrough: PS stands for postscript, a note added at the end of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is something appended to a document, just as a postscript is added after the signature.

clue.text: Dead bird komodo dragon's eaten, brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up reads its letters from bottom to top
what is eaten sits inside, so the letters lie within the words around it

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A dead bird swallowed by a komodo dragon and then regurgitated.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless bird of Mauritius is extinct, the classic example of a species wiped out.

clue.text: Art's models represented by these!

indicators.note: to be represented is to be presented again in a different form, so the letters are recast

parts.note: every letter of these words, possessive S included

explanation.surface: Artists' sitters were painted by the great painters of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the great painters did paint models.
explanation.definitionFit: Great European painters of earlier centuries depicted models in their works, so they portrayed artists' sitters.

clue.text: Nebuchadnezzar, extremely welcoming Old Testament figure? In no degree!

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so the outer letters enclose another piece
extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the Babylonian king's name
the first woman in Genesis; the question mark flags her as one example

explanation.surface: Would King Nebuchadnezzar ever take in a biblical character? Certainly not!
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means not at all, not to any extent, which is what 'in no degree' says.

clue.text: 'Everyman's superseded': note in chronicle that's brutal

indicators.note: to be superseded is to be replaced, so one letter is swapped out for another piece

parts.note: an annal is a year-by-year record
N is the abbreviation for note
the setter speaking of himself: I am, shortened

explanation.surface: The setter complains of being sidelined in a chronicle that sounds cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman is the setter, so 'Everyman's' stands for I'M; it takes the place of the second N in the chronicle.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes base, physical, beastly behaviour, so savage or brutal conduct.

clue.text: Scientist Darwin gets in a muddle with dishrack

indicators.note: a muddle is a confused mess, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Charles Darwin gets tangled up in the kitchen dishrack.
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin looks like the scientist being defined, but he is only fodder; the definition is the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawkins is a British evolutionary biologist, author of The Selfish Gene and a noted populariser of science.

clue.text: Demented broadcast with no time to be edited

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
with no says the following item is left out

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A frantic broadcast, rushed out without time to correct it.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and revise it, so it describes something that has been corrected.

clue.text: Having no time or energy, distractedly vindicate historical figure

indicators.note: doing something distractedly means doing it in a confused way, so the letters are jumbled
having no means lacking, so the named items are taken away

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
E is the symbol for energy in physics
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone short of time and energy absentmindedly clears a famous figure's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci, the Renaissance painter and inventor, is one of history's best-known people.

clue.text: Endlessly desiring friendly words from driver

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to hope for something is to desire it

explanation.surface: A driver's kindly offer of a lift to someone longing to get home.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist offering a lift says this casual invitation, telling a pedestrian to climb aboard.

clue.text: In retrospect, 'sound of approval' politician claimed? It's a sound of disapproval

indicators.note: something claimed is taken in and held, so one piece goes inside the other
looking in retrospect means looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cheer of approval
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Looking back, a politician claimed applause, but really got grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets up approval against disapproval: the cheer, turned round, becomes its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the gruff throat-clearing noise of a pompous person expressing displeasure or disagreement.

clue.text: Instant urge to get IT gismo

parts.note: a flash is an instant
a drive is an inner urge

explanation.surface: An immediate craving to buy the latest computer gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A USB memory stick is a small computer gadget for storing and moving files, so information technology kit.

clue.text: Head hurt? Let's get together some food

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
a cut is a hurt
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a sore head suggests meeting up for a bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: These are vegetarian patties made from chopped nuts, breadcrumbs and seasoning, so an item of food.

clue.text: Primarily, smear, libel, undo reputations?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: the initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: The main aim of smearing and libelling is to ruin reputations.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: such attacks do damage reputations.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insinuation or slander, whose purpose is to damage someone's good name.

clue.text: Show's host appears after 500 commercials

indicators.note: appearing after means following, so the first piece named is placed at the end

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
commercials are advertisements
a host is a great army

explanation.surface: A TV presenter comes on after hundreds of adverts.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic British TV sitcom about the wartime Home Guard. Host here is the old word for an army, not a presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long-running BBC sitcom, a television programme or show, still regularly repeated.

clue.text: Anarchist, to some extent, is mischievous

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the word is used

parts.note: the letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: An anarchist is a bit of a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means playfully knowing and roguish, as in an arch smile.

clue.text: Perhaps to keep a Persian in attic's wrong

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: every letter, possessive S included

explanation.surface: Shutting a Persian away in the attic would be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Persian looks like a person or a rug, but it is a breed of cat; 'Perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after someone's pet while they are away is the job, and a Persian is one kind of pet.

clue.text: In line with plan, a second place in Scotland revoked degree

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: revoked means called back, so the word is taken back to front

parts.note: DEG is the abbreviation for degree

explanation.surface: As planned, a runner-up in Scotland has a qualification withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means according to what was agreed or planned beforehand, so in line with the plan.

clue.text: On the radio, an insurgent ape

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so a word spelt differently but sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: a guerrilla is an irregular insurgent fighter

explanation.surface: A radio report of a rebel ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the great apes, native to central African forests.

clue.text: Delivered by Spooner, rug prepared in old Asian capital

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial consonants trade places

parts.note: a rug is a mat and prepared is can-do, ready and willing

explanation.surface: A rug ready-made in a historic city in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of the two words and they become cat man-do. Katmandu is an older spelling of Kathmandu, capital of Nepal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kathmandu is the capital city of Nepal, and Katmandu is the older, traditional spelling of its name.

clue.text: Ampere: unit giving current

parts.note: A is the symbol for the ampere
a foot is a unit of length

explanation.surface: An ampere being a unit that measures electric current.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about electricity, but current here means happening now.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afoot is going on or in progress, so current in the sense of under way now.

clue.text: Fast-food freebie recalled, growths found on skin

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: warts are small skin growths

explanation.surface: A fast-food giveaway withdrawn after customers developed skin growths.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking tubes are handed out free with fizzy drinks at burger chains, a giveaway item.

clue.text: Band's promotional material is abridged

indicators.note: abridged means cut short, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a blurb is a short promotional description

explanation.surface: A group's publicity material has been shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur is a British rock band, famous in the 1990s Britpop era.
explanation.definitionFit: Blur is the name of a well-known British rock group from the Britpop years, so a musical group.

clue.text: Perhaps McKellan's comeback: singer contracted in safari destination

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Ian McKellen is the actor; Perhaps flags one example of the first name

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: the robin is a songbird

explanation.surface: An actor's return to the stage, with a singer cut short, at a safari spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya's capital is the usual starting point for safaris in East Africa, a destination for tourists.

clue.text: Charmer is lovelier, not very unreliable

indicators.note: unreliable letters cannot be trusted to stay put, so they are rearranged
not says the following item is to be left out

parts.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A seductive charmer is lovely but not to be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lorelei is the siren of German legend who lured Rhine boatmen to their doom with her singing.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a legendary siren whose singing enchanted sailors, an alluring enchantress or temptress.

clue.text: Sat idly, years wasted: there's still time!

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined, so its letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: every letter of these words

explanation.surface: Someone who has lazed away the years is told it is not too late.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a situation is at an early stage, so there remains plenty of opportunity ahead.
